$comment: A derived template (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): the care pack composed with a marriage & family therapy content seed and a warm clay brand over the luxe-light register. Everything else — pages, sections, contract, tests — is the base pack's; compose expands this catalog through resolveCatalog (scripts/lib/pack-switch.mjs).
title: Marriage & family therapist
description: A marriage & family therapy practice site built to feel like the waiting room: therapist bios with credentials, services for couples, families, and teens, plain-language FAQs on cost and confidentiality, an in-network insurance strip, evening hours, and real online session booking — free consultations, intakes, and 50-minute sessions projected from each therapist's actual week, capacity-1, double-booking impossible. The booking form is deliberately clinically empty: name, contact, session type — what brings you in never touches the site.

content.$comment: Business-content contract seed override. resolveCatalog merges a remix's content per-domain over the base's, so these practice and appointments seeds replace the base pack's at compose and mirror THIS remix's contentSeed module entry for entry (the remix-seed tests pin the twins) — the composed template's Manage editors and booking widget open on the therapy practice, not the base clinic.

providers.name: Dr. Maya Brennan
providers.bio: Eighteen years of couples work, trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy and Gottman Method Level 3. Maya founded Stillwater around one belief: the relationship is the client. She's direct, warm, and unafraid of the hard conversation you've been avoiding.

providers.name: Sam Delgado
providers.bio: Sam works with whole families and the teenagers in them — school refusal, blended-family friction, the silence at the dinner table. Structural family therapy, a decade of school-counseling experience, and sessions in English or Spanish.

providers.name: Ruth Okafor
providers.bio: Ruth sees the individuals inside family systems — new parents, adult children of aging parents, anyone carrying a loss. Clients describe her as the calmest hour of their week. ACT and narrative therapy, with homework you'll actually do.

services.name: Couples therapy
services.description: Weekly 50-minute sessions for couples at any stage — gridlocked conflict, rebuilding trust, or a strong marriage you want to keep that way.

services.name: Family therapy
services.description: The whole household in one room, working on the patterns between people rather than blaming any one of them.

services.name: Individual therapy
services.description: One-on-one work on anxiety, life transitions, and the relationships you bring with you — because individuals live in systems too.

services.name: Teen & adolescent therapy
services.description: A place for 13-to-18-year-olds that isn't the principal's office — with parents involved exactly as much as helps.

services.name: Premarital counseling
services.description: Six structured sessions before the wedding: money, family, conflict, and the conversations easier to have now than at year five.

services.name: Parenting support
services.description: Practical, judgment-free coaching for the season you're in — toddler storms, co-parenting after divorce, launching young adults.

services.name: Grief & loss
services.description: Room to grieve at your own pace — a death, a divorce, a diagnosis — with a therapist who won't rush you to the silver lining.

services.name: Telehealth sessions
services.description: Secure video sessions anywhere in Wisconsin, for the weeks when getting to Monroe Street is the obstacle.

reviews.quote: We came in barely speaking and planning who'd keep the house. Two years later we still do our Thursday check-ins from the worksheets Dr. Brennan gave us. She saved us the hard way — by making us do the work.
reviews.name: J. & M.

reviews.quote: Sam is the first counselor our son didn't stonewall. He talked to him like a person, not a problem, and taught the rest of us to do the same.
reviews.name: The K. family

reviews.quote: Ruth sat with me through the worst year of my life and never once handed me a platitude. That hour was the one place I didn't have to be okay.
reviews.name: A. R.

newPatient.title: Do you take insurance?
newPatient.body: We're in network with the plans listed above, and for everything else we provide a superbill for out-of-network reimbursement. Session fees are on the confirmation email — no surprises at the door.

newPatient.title: What happens in the first session?
newPatient.body: Mostly, you talk and we listen: what's bringing you in, what you've tried, what better would look like. You'll leave with a plan — how often we'll meet, what we're working toward, and how we'll know it's working.

newPatient.title: How long does therapy take?
newPatient.body: It depends on the work, and you'll always know where we are. Many couples come weekly for three to six months, then taper. We review goals every eight sessions — staying is a choice we make together, never a default.

newPatient.title: Is what we say confidential?
newPatient.body: Yes, with the legal exceptions every therapist carries (safety, court orders), which we'll walk through in plain language before you say a word. Booking online asks nothing about your story — that stays in the room.

types.name: Free 15-minute consultation
types.description: A short phone call to see whether we're the right fit — no charge, no pressure.

types.name: First session (intake)
types.description: A longer first session: your story, your goals, and a plan for the work.

types.name: Therapy session
types.description: The standard 50-minute session — individual, couples, or family.

theme.$comment: Warm clay over the luxe-light register's near-white ground — the care family's calm, credible light voice re-inked from clinical teal to the therapy room's terracotta. mode light opens the site in its native daylight appearance; marketing pages resolve brand over preset accent, so the overlay re-inks pages and app surfaces together. navigation re-pins the shared careShell chrome (a declared theme variant outranks the shell prop): the base clinic wears the full-width administrative band, so the therapy practice takes the centered masthead — the warmer, more editorial read — per the nav-variety audit.
